2_Introduction: By interlinking experimental conditions with device architecture, a perovskite solar cell was fabricated, affirming a PCE of 25.7614%, FF of 84.8668%, Voc of 1.1862 V, and Jsc of 25.59 mA/cm². The Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 perovskite precursor (1.65 mol/L) was spin-coated onto the substrate. A meticulously timed spin procedure included 1000 rpm for 5 s, succeeded by 5500 rpm for 30 s to refine crystal growth. A total of 150 µL of CB was dripped onto the center of film at 15 s before the end of spin-coating. Thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 min improved crystal ordering and reduced defect density.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite layer—engineered with a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture—exhibits enhanced phase stability and suppressed halide segregation due to the synergistic tolerance factor modulation by formamidinium (FA⁺) as the dominant cation, methylammonium (MA⁺) for lattice strain relaxation, and cesium (Cs⁺) for thermal and phase stability, while the stoichiometric PbI₃.₀ composition minimizes iodide vacancies and suppresses deep-level trap formation; its crystallization is precisely governed by the dual-speed spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 5 s) enabling uniform precursor wetting and nucleation onset, followed by high-speed (5500 rpm, 30 s) inducing rapid solvent evaporation and controlled supersaturation—wherein the antisolvent quenching with 150 µL chlorobenzene at 15 s prior to spin termination critically arrests Ostwald ripening, promotes homogeneous nucleation density, and stabilizes the δ-to-α phase transition pathway, thereby yielding large, oriented grains with reduced grain boundary area and suppressed non-radiative recombination centers; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 min further drives out residual solvent, heals interfacial voids, relieves lattice strain evidenced by narrowed XRD peak FWHM and absence of parasitic PbI₂ (12.6°), and consolidates crystallographic coherence across the film—collectively reflected in high spatial uniformity of PL intensity mapping, minimal grayscale heterogeneity in optical micrographs indicating near-complete film coverage, and monoexponential PL decay kinetics with extended lifetime (>1.2 µs), all corroborating low defect density, suppressed trap-assisted recombination, and efficient charge extraction across uninterrupted transport pathways; these morphological, optical, and structural advantages are intrinsically coupled to interfacial energetics and defect passivation, though no exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators were introduced, meaning intrinsic defect mitigation arises solely from compositional optimization, kinetic crystallization control, and thermally activated defect annihilation—resulting in VOC of 1.1862 V, JSC of 25.59 mA/cm², FF of 84.8668%, and PCE of 25.7614%.
